extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED), and disciplinary enforcement agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order imposing reciprocal exclusion from practice before the USPTO based on a state-court permanent disbarment, describing procedural steps, required notifications, and the professional-conduct violations that formed the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Director may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a State (here, permanent disbarment by the Supreme Court of Ohio). The Notice and Order requested that the Director impose reciprocal discipline identical to the Ohio order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice and Order is sent and the respondent is given an opportunity to oppose within the time period provided in § 11.24(d)(1). If no timely response creates a genuine issue of material fact, reciprocal discipline identical to the State discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent excluded for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being permanently disbarred from the practice of law by a duly constituted State authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order identifies the regulatory provision violated as the basis for exclusion; the state disbarment supplies the predicate facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (certified mail, publication, 40-day period)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' was sent by certified mail and published in the Official Gazette, providing Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: certified mailing and public notice; respondent must timely file any opposition raising reasons under § 11.24(d)(1) to prevent automatic reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for 'no genuine issue of material fact' under § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, it is determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond to the Notice supports a determination that reciprocal discipline identical to the State's discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative requirement to make the Final Order publicly available via the OED FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette Notice content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion, including the respondent's name, registration number, basis for exclusion (violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) predicated upon permanent disbarment), and a summary of the facts and rules violated as conveyed in the state-court opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Gazette notice must summarize the misconduct findings (conflicts, practicing while suspended, failure to respond to investigation, false communications) and list the specific rules of professional conduct the state court found violated; include reference to OED FOIA Reading Room decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative duty to inform relevant jurisdictions and institutions of the USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's duties under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-discipline obligations (e.g., notice to clients, withdrawal from practice tasks, complying with administrative requirements) as specified in § 11.58 must be followed by the excluded practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer and USPTO verified Electronic System Accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System Account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational step to prevent the excluded practitioner from appearing as associated with clients or electronic accounts on USPTO systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for action: 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory and regulatory authority authorizing USPTO reciprocal discipline based on state court disbarment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing clients with directly adverse interests (Ohio Rule 1.7(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a lawyer's continued representation of a client if the representation of that client will be directly adverse to another client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-court found respondent represented clients with adverse interests in violation of this rule; such conduct supports discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest risk standard (Ohio Rule 1.7(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A lawyer's continued representation creates a conflict of interest if there is a substantial risk that the lawyer's ability to represent the client will be materially limited by responsibilities to another client, former client, third person, or by the lawyer's own personal interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-court found respondent's representations created such substantial risks, contributing to disbarment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting/continuing representation with unconsentable conflict (Ohio Rule 1.7(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a lawyer from accepting or continuing representation if such representation would create a conflict of interest, unless the lawyer can competently and diligently represent each affected client, each gives informed consent in writing, and the representation is not otherwise prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Ohio decision found respondent failed to obtain required written informed consents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on representing clients when one client asserts claim against another client (Ohio Rule 1.7(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits accepting or continuing a representation if the representation would involve the assertion of a claim by one client against another client represented by the lawyer in the same proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-court factual findings included such conflicts among clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on business transactions with clients (Ohio Rule 1.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a lawyer from entering into a business transaction with a client or knowingly acquiring an ownership, possessory, security, or other pecuniary interest adverse to a client unless (1) terms are fair and fully disclosed in writing, (2) client is advised in writing to obtain independent counsel, and (3) client gives informed consent in a writing signed by the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-court determined respondent engaged in improper business dealings with clients without satisfying these protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational-client representation duties (Ohio Rule 1.13(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A lawyer employed or retained by an organization represents the organization acting through its constituents and owes allegiance to the organization and not to its constituents or any other person connected with the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper allegiances to individuals rather than the organization can form a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of organization constituents (Ohio Rule 1.13(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A lawyer representing an organization may also represent any of its directors, officers, employees, members, shareholders, or other constituents, subject to the consent requirements of Gov. Bar R. 1.7; if written consent is required, it must be given by an appropriate official of the organization, not by the individual to be represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-court found respondent failed to adhere to organizational consent requirements when representing constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicing law in a jurisdiction in violation of regulation (Ohio Rule 5.5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a lawyer from practicing law in a jurisdiction in violation of the regulation of the legal profession in that jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Ohio court found respondent continued to practice while suspended, violating this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (Ohio Rule 8.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a lawyer from engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings that respondent falsely communicated lawyer's services and held himself out as authorized to practice supported violation of this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond to disciplinary authority (Ohio Rule 8.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a lawyer from knowingly failing to respond to a demand for information by a disciplinary authority during an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ohio court found respondent failed to respond to a disciplinary investigation, a ground for disbarment and reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on false or misleading communications about lawyer or services (Ohio Rule 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a lawyer from making or using false, misleading, or nonverifiable communication about the lawyer or the lawyer's services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-court determined respondent continued to hold himself out as an attorney authorized to practice in Ohio, constituting false communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific misconduct findings supporting discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of factual findings: represented clients with adverse interests; represented clients with conflicts of interest without obtaining written informed consent; continued to practice law while under suspension; failed to respond to a disciplinary investigation; continued to hold himself out as authorized to practice law in Ohio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factual misconduct findings (as set forth in the Ohio slip opinion) formed the predicate for the state's permanent disbarment and the USPTO's reciprocal exclusion.
